dedupe_keys.name: florida statewide regional evacuation study storm surge zones florida division of emergency management 2021

description: This dataset contains the storm surge zones used for hurricane evacuation planning in Florida, produced by the Florida Division of Emergency Management for the Florida Statewide Regional Evacuation Study Update and distributed by the Florida Geographic Data Library. The zones were built with a surge modelling application from the National Hurricane Center's SLOSH model runs for every NOAA SLOSH basin in Florida: the maximum of maximums envelope of water for each storm category 1 to 5 was intersected with a LIDAR digital elevation model at 5-foot resolution and contiguous shoreline polygons, so that each polygon shows the land that category of storm could flood. Coverage is the whole Florida coast, in the August 2021 version, as vector polygons. The data are free to download from the Florida Geographic Data Library as a US state government product with its metadata. Caveats: zones are worst-case planning envelopes, not forecasts for a given storm, the shoreline used dates from 2004, and county evacuation zones may differ from surge zones. Simulation uses: defining populations and facilities such as hospitals and nursing homes that must evacuate, building evacuation demand for traffic and shelter models, and hazard exposure screening for Florida infrastructure. Related records: NYC hurricane evacuation zones (data-nyc-hurricane-evacuation-zones) serve the same purpose for New York, and OpenFEMA (data-openfema) records past disaster declarations.
